newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury minister gets tough on pensions chiefs.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury minister gets tough on pensions chiefs.

text.p: Britain's Economic Secretary to the Treasury on Wednesday delivered an ultimatum to life companies over compensating the victims of pension misselling.
The companies face regulatory and public pressure to speed up their reviews of pensions misselling in the late 1980s and early 1990s
As many as half a million people may have been wrongly advised to opt out of occupational pensions schemes in favour of personal pensions.
Helen Liddell met with senior managers of 28 companies and gave them a month to report back to her on progress made. She also plans to publish regular updates on their progress.
"The delay in providing redress for the victims of misselling is simply unacceptable. Investment firms have seriously underestimated the depth of public anger about this," she said in a statement.
Liddell said it was ordinary people who were being hurt by the "foot dragging" of the companies. She said the new Labour government found this unacceptable and it would not be tolerated.

"The public interest now demands that all the firms responsible act swiftly. Let there be no misunderstanding," she said, adding her backing for targets published by regulator the Personal Investment Authority (PIA) on Tuesday.

Failure to deliver would have serious consequences for the industry and if firms were not able to convince the Treasury of their sincerity in completing reviews and providing compensation they would face the consequences, she said.
Liddell also said the government would take their conduct into account in its reform of financial services regulation, which it promised before it was elected on May 1.
